1: Chapter 1: A Guest in the Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. In the spring, Anna Weber’s older sister had gone to Berlin, and since then Anna had been running the village’s small pharmacy alone.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day’s takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when there was a loud knocking at the door downstairs. A man’s voice called out: “Is anyone there?”
Outside stood a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need a bandage,” Wolf whispered. “I can pay. Would three thousand five hundred marks be enough?”
He pulled an oil‑paper‑wrapped letter from his jacket. “This letter has to be at Steinbach Monastery before May 18.”
She must have had her head in the clouds: only now did she notice how pale he was.
Still, she wouldn’t take his money and said only, “I’ll take you up into the mountains first thing tomorrow.”
2: At daybreak they set off. Anna carried a basket on her back with bread, healing herbs, and an old umbrella.
Halfway up they met the old Hans Becker, who was chopping wood. He set his axe aside and whispered that last night three strangers had asked at the village entrance about an injured young man.
"Take the path, Anna," said Hans Becker. "The country road isn’t safe." Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna went ahead, placing each step carefully. Wolf followed her silently.
By midday the rain had stopped, the fog began to lift, and in the distance the roof of Steinbach Abbey came into view. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who welcomed guests at the abbey.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Wolf said to Anna: "I owe you my life." Anna smiled: "Then next time repair the roof of my pharmacy." Wolf stayed at the abbey.
In the evening Anna went down the mountain alone. When she got home it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat a long while behind the counter.
